desk.headline: Revenue up 40% to $174.1m, beat; full-year revenue range narrowed to $665–681m with a higher midpoint
results: Revenue rose 40% to $174.1m: subscriptions up 29% to $124.2m and advertising more than tripled to $25.4m after the Nativo purchase; hardware fell 20% to $9.0m after exiting store retail.
Paying Circles grew by a third-quarter record 188k to 3.4m (+26%); monthly users reached 107.7m, with international users up 21% to 51.9m.
Net income was $22.5m ($0.26 per diluted share) versus $9.8m, helped by a $17.5m investment gain; adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $34.6m.
Gross margin slipped to 77% from 78% on lower-margin advertising; operating costs rose 38% but fell to 72% of revenue from 80% in Q2.
Operating cash flow was $27.2m; cash and short-term investments $465.0m; $31.2m of shares bought back in the quarter, $180.6m left on the programme.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 revenue range tightened to $665–681m (from $650–685m), lifting the midpoint; subscription and other revenue raised, advertising top end cut, adjusted EBITDA narrowed to $132–138m and user growth unchanged.

points: CEO says early results from US subscription price rises are "encouraging"; average revenue per Paying Circle rose 4%.
Advertising is described as a foundation built in 2026, with brand wins giving positive signals for 2027.
The company is opening its family data to outside AI assistants, with members choosing whether to share.
CFO expects Q4 revenue momentum from price rises and seasonal advertising, with lower growth-media spend lifting margins.
Buybacks are meant to offset share dilution from staff stock awards over a rolling 12 months.
call.source: Management comments in the press release and investor presentation (Exhibits 99.1, 99.3); no call coverage found

watch: Effect of US price increases on Paying Circle additions and cancellations in Q4.
Whether advertising reaches the $98–102m full-year range after the top end was cut, and the 2027 ad build-out.
Delivery of the roughly 20% adjusted EBITDA margin and further operating-cost leverage.
